sections.title: Standards nobody loads
body: Teams write conventions down, then rely on everyone, and every assistant, remembering them. They don’t. The same correction gets typed again next week.

sections.title: Four levels, strongest first
body: Every rule has an enforcement level: mandatory, required, recommended or advisory. A mandatory rule is locked: a narrower scope may refine it but never weaken it.
points: Then the most specific scope wins

sections.title: From organization to repository
body: Rules attach at scopes such as organization, client, team, technology, project and repository. The more specific scope refines the broader one, and duplicates collapse to the highest authority.

sections.title: Loaded, not remembered
body: The assistant calls Sensei’s get_rules and layered-context tools at session start and after context compaction, so the resolved rules are in front of it while it works.
